newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Elf oil find in Angola could be Africa's biggest.
newsitem.headline: Elf oil find in Angola could be Africa's biggest.

text.p: An offshore oil find in Angola by Elf Aquitaine could be one of the biggest in Africa and hold in excess of 500 to 700 million barrels of reserves, an Elf Exploration Angola official said on Tuesday.
Elf said earlier on Tuesday that the new find was made in the Dalia field in Block 17 in a water depth of 1,360 metres about three km from the Girassol well announced in April 1996.
Bernard Astier, Elf Exploration Angola assistant director general, told Reuters the potential of the new find was fantastic.
"It is perfectly possible that this is the biggest offshore find yet in Africa. The seismic work shows this particular area to be fantastic," Astier said.
Elf said in an earlier statement that production tests gave a cumulative flow rate of 16,000 barrels per day. Further appraisals have to be carried out to evaluate the commercial potential.
Girassol 1 was the company's first discovery well.
"Girassol was a very good find. It has between 500 to 700 million barrels of reserves, but we think the Dalia find is better," Astier said.
He said his optimism was not based on speculation but on scientific data.

"Of course we need to do more tests to make sure. But we are confident it is something big, and we base our feelings on our experience in Block 17, but also on our seismic data which looks very good."

Elf Exploration, a joint venture between the French oil company Elf Aquitaine and the Angolan state oil company Sonangol, is the operator of the Block 17 drilling licence and holds a 35 percent stake in the block.
Other partners in Block 17 are Esso Exploration Angola, BP Exploration (Angola), Den Norske Stats Oljeselkskap ASA (Statoil), Norsk Hydro and Fina Exploration M.B.V.
Angola is Africa's fifth-largest oil producer and analysts see the country's oil and gas potential as enormous.
